question: Does a shared representation with stage-specific heads outperform a single pooled stage-aware model for dynamic Lead Quality scoring?
hypothesis: A shared backbone with separately calibrated T0, T1 and T2 heads will improve ranking or calibration because the meaning and information set of the lead changes materially across funnel stages.
primary_change: shared neural backbone with T0/T1/T2 stage-specific probability heads
secondary_changes: moving 30-day target anchored at each scoring timestamp
point-in-time historical interaction features for engaged leads

scoring_time.timestamp_definition: T0=leads.created_at; T1=first inquiries.inquiry_at; T2=second and later inquiries.inquiry_at while no scheduled_visit has already occurred

population.eligibility: Scoring snapshots with a complete 30-day future observation window; T1/T2 are generated only before a known scheduled visit has occurred.
exclusions: Dynamic snapshots after an already observed scheduled visit.
Current/future broker-response information from model inputs.

validation.split_description: Chronological 70/15/15 split by lead creation; every T0/T1/T2 snapshot for a lead is assigned to the same partition. Validation controls early stopping and calibration; test is untouched until final evaluation.

items.evidence: Only fields stored on the lead row at creation are used; lead_score_internal is explicitly blocked.
The current inquiry payload is available when the inquiry arrives; broker response outcome/timing is excluded from predictors.
Only static listing/attribute fields are used. Mutable snapshot-like columns days_on_market, total_inquiries, total_views and is_active are excluded.

items.source: derived from lead, current inquiry and static spot fields
items.evidence: Ratios and equality/compatibility flags use only point-in-time-safe source fields.
Backward as-of join forbids snapshots after the scoring timestamp.

items.source: prior inquiries and already-realized broker responses
items.evidence: Prior response features require inferred response_event_at=inquiry_at+broker_response_hours <= scoring_time; current and future response information is excluded.
Stage is determined only by whether the lead is at creation, first inquiry, or later pre-conversion inquiry at the scoring timestamp.
